# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your money trail, not blank pages** — Pull last month's billing/class data. What are members actually paying for NOW? Which services generate 60%+ of revenue? Build your menu around what's proven, then add gaps. Don't invent offerings—validate them first.

• **Split into two documents with different angles.** Coach version = operational clarity (what CAN they sell, commission structure, upsell triggers). Member version = benefit-focused language (not just "Personal Training — £40/hr" but "1-on-1 Strength Plan — £40/session — 12-week transformation included"). Coaches need to know profitability; members need to feel outcome.

• **Price anchoring move** — If you're unsure on pricing, don't guess. Run a quick email to your engaged members (top 20% attendance): "What would you pay for [specific service]?" You'll get real ceiling data in 48 hours. Use that to position—not undercut competitors, but to justify YOUR value clearly on the menu.

• **Make it a sales tool immediately** — Print physical menus for reception, create a simple 1-page PDF for WhatsApp/email. Don't let this sit in a doc. Put it in front of members this week during peak hours. Track which services members ask about—that tells you what to push harder.

• **Lock in your margin math now** — For each service, note: cost to deliver it, margin target (usually 60-70% for services), and minimum monthly volume needed to hit targets. This prevents pricing yourself into corners later.
